full_judgment: 6. Mr. M. A. Khaled, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, submitted that since the petitioners have claimed the ownership as well as the right of management of the Mazar since its inception, being not only the Khadims but also being related To the Saint, the respondents had no right To issue the said notices and form a Committee of management of the Mazar in pursuance thereof. There are no provisions of law which empowered them To interfere with the right the petitioners have been exercising for last 55 years. In support of the proposition that for every order passed by a member of the executive there must be a law authorising him To do so, the learned Advocate cited a decision reported in 14 D.L.R. (Dac.) 874. In dealing with a similar question whether an order of the Sub-Divisional Officer, (North), Chittagong which required the removal of unauthorised construction from the site of the Railway premises, Chittagong was valid and legal without the basis of some laws and which came To be considered in this case, Murshed J, as he then was, observed that even if the Railway could, establish its title To the land, the Sub-Divisional Officer has no jurisdiction To pass the order of removal. Thus, it was patent that the Sub-Divisional Officer, purported To act as a Court and this is apparent not merely from the manner and form in which the order has been couched but also from the order itself. According To him, the order on the proper analysis amounts To a decree passed in a suit for ejectment. In refuting the assertion that the order passed by the Sub-Divisional Officer was merely an executive order and was justified, Murshed J, pronounced categorically against the soundness of the proposition advanced as above.
